accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Basin — State
1. Cambay — Gujarat
2. Krishna-Godavari — Andhra Pradesh
3. Cauvery — Tamil Nadu
4. Rajasthan Basin — Rajasthan
accepted.x: Cambay is in Gujarat, Krishna-Godavari in Andhra Pradesh, Cauvery in Tamil Nadu and the Barmer-Jaisalmer basin in Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Use the state-basin association and eliminate options containing a swapped location.
accepted.sec: Sedimentary basins and gas fields - state and category  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ankleshwar and Kalol are important fields of which sedimentary basin?
accepted.x: Ankleshwar and Kalol are key fields of the Cambay Basin in Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Test the field-to-basin association directly.
accepted.sec: Sedimentary basins and gas fields - state and category  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bombay High is associated with which one of the following basins?
accepted.x: Bombay High is the principal field associated with the Mumbai Offshore Basin off the Maharashtra coast. It was developed after the 1973 oil shock.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a well-known offshore field from onshore basin fields.
accepted.sec: Sedimentary basins and gas fields - state and category  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding petroleum occurrence is correct?
o: Oil is formed only in Precambrian rocks and occurs chiefly in river valleys.
Oil is formed mainly in the Quaternary period and occurs only in volcanic rocks.
Oil formed in the Tertiary period, and most reserves occur in anticlines and fault traps.
Oil formed in the Jurassic period and is confined exclusively to synclines.
accepted.x: The material identifies the Tertiary period as the period of oil formation and anticlines and fault traps as the principal settings of most reserves.
accepted.tq: Combine the geological age with the structural-trap concept in the precise option.
accepted.sec: Sedimentary basins and gas fields - state and category  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Shale gas and oil are primarily held in
o: permeable sandstone and extracted without stimulation
coal seams and released mainly by pumping water
fine-grained shale and generally require hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling
accepted.x: Shale hydrocarbons occur in fine-grained shale and require fracking and horizontal drilling. Coal seams hold coal bed methane, while gas hydrates occur as methane-water crystals.
accepted.tq: Discriminate unconventional resources by their host formation and extraction method.
accepted.sec: Unconventional hydrocarbons - shale gas, CBM, gas hydrates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Coal bed methane is best described as methane that is
o: adsorbed in coal seams and released by pumping water
dissolved in seawater and frozen below the seabed
mixed with propane and butane during petroleum refining
trapped in permeable sandstone and extracted by ordinary wells
accepted.x: Coal bed methane is methane held or adsorbed in coal seams and is released by pumping out water.
accepted.tq: Separate CBM from shale gas and gas hydrates by identifying both its host and release method.
accepted.sec: Unconventional hydrocarbons - shale gas, CBM, gas hydrates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first commercial output of coal bed methane in India was obtained at
accepted.x: The first commercial output of coal bed methane was obtained at Raniganj. Jharia, Bokaro and Sohagpur are also important CBM areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first commercial site from the wider list of CBM areas.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes conventional gas from unconventional gas?
o: Conventional gas occurs in impermeable shale only, whereas unconventional gas occurs in permeable sandstone only.
Conventional gas generally occurs in permeable sandstone, whereas unconventional gas occurs in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams and requires costly technology.
Both types occur only in coal seams and are extracted by pumping water.
Neither type requires drilling or specialised technology.
accepted.x: Conventional gas is found in permeable sandstone. Unconventional gas occurs in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams and generally needs costly extraction technology.
accepted.tq: Compare the host formations and technological requirements rather than the fuel name alone.
accepted.sec: Unconventional hydrocarbons - shale gas, CBM, gas hydrates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding LNG, CNG and LPG?
o: LNG is natural gas cooled below −160°C; CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm²; LPG mainly contains propane and butane.
LNG is propane cooled below −16°C; CNG is compressed to 20–25 kg/cm²; LPG mainly contains methane.
LNG and LPG are identical forms of methane, while CNG is a mixture of propane and butane.
LNG is coal bed methane, whereas LPG is methane frozen in deep-sea sediments.
accepted.x: LNG is methane-rich natural gas cooled below −160°C, CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm², and LPG mainly consists of propane and butane from refining.
accepted.tq: Separate the three similar fuel terms using their state, pressure and composition.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of the dates or years associated with them:

A. Proposal of a national gas grid by S. H. Zaheer
B. Beginning of One Nation One Gas Grid
C. Establishment of IIPE Visakhapatnam
D. IIPE becoming an Institute of National Importance

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The order is 1955 proposal, 2014 beginning of ONOGG, 2016 establishment of IIPE and 2017 recognition as an Institute of National Importance. However, among the provided options, the sequence that places A before C, D and B is not chronologically accurate because B precedes C and D.
